name: Ivar Tollefsen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Real estate investor Ivar Tollefsen started his first company at age 14, Tollefsen Enterprises, which rented out DJ-services and event equipment.
With the earnings from his disco business he began building a real estate empire, now called Fredensborg AS.
Fredensborg owns 150,000 apartments across Europe and, in 2017, bought an Oslo building that used to house the U.S. embassy.
Tollefsen has led several polar expeditions and has competed in the Dakar Rally.

name: Travis Kalanick
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Travis Kalanick cofounded ride-hailing firm Uber in 2009.
Kalanick stepped down as CEO in 2017 and left the board in 2019.
He sold all his Uber stock for more than $2.5 billion (pretax) in 2019.
He is now CEO of CloudKitchens, a global virtual kitchen company that raised money from Microsoft and the Saudi sovereign wealth fund.
Kalanick cofounded two tech startups before Uber: online file-exchange service Scour and file-sharing company RedSwoosh.
forbes_facts: Kalanick dropped out of UCLA in 1998 to work on Scour full-time with some classmates.
Scour was later sued by the Motion Picture Association of America and the Recording Industry Association of America before filing for bankruptcy in 2000.

name: Vildan Gulcelik
forbes_bio: Vildan Gulcelik is one of more than a dozen family members who hold shares in ENKA, one of Turkey's largest construction and energy companies.

ENKA, which was cofounded in 1957 by Sarik Tara and his brother-in-law, Sadi Gulcelik, is Turkey's leading private electricity producer and also operates in real estate, tourism, transport and trade (construction equipment and machinery).
In Moscow, ENKA owns a hotel, shopping malls and approximately 370,000 square meters of net rentable Class A office space.
Sadi Gulcelik died in a plane accident in Saudi Arabia in 1980, and Mehmet Sinan Tara took over in 1984 at age 26. His son Agah Mehmet Tara became CEO in 2012, at age 29.
forbes_facts: Over the last 20 years or so, ENKA has been the biggest builder of U.S. consular and embassy buildings.
These government projects can be found in locations ranging from Turkey, Algeria and Nepal to Equatorial Guinea, the Dominican Republic and the Netherlands.

name: Lucy Peng
forbes_bio: Lucy Lei Peng was a director of financial technology firm Ant Group from 2013 until August 2020.
Peng has previously been chief people officer at Alibaba Group, and held other positions at the company as well.
Peng graduated from Hangzhou Institute of Commerce of Zhejiang Gongshang University in 1994 with a bachelor's degree in business administration.
China held up Ant's planned dual listing in Shanghai and Hong Kong on regulatory concerns on Nov. 3, 2020.

name: Kiril Domuschiev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Kiril Domuschiev is the co-owner, alongside his brother Georgi, of Bulgarian investment conglomerate Advance Properties.
Founded in 2003, Advance Properties has interests in animal health, shipping, port management, real estate and soccer.
Advance's largest asset is Huvepharma, the world's sixth-largest livestock health company, which has factories in four countries including the U.S.
The Domuschiev brothers started out selling locally manufactured shoes in the 1990s and then started investing in privatized state-owned companies.
They also owned Bulgaria's largest media TV network, Nova TV, from February 2019 to January 2021, when they sold it for $340 million.

name: Tarek Mansour
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: Tarek Mansour is the cofounder and CEO of prediction markets firm Kalshi.

Kalshi allows users to bet on everything from sports game results to political elections to entertainment awards and more. It reached a $11 billion valuation in December 2025 following a $1 billion funding round.

Kalshi received federal approval in 2020 to operate in the U.S., and made history in 2024 after receiving federal approval to allow users to bet on the presidential election, marking the first legal election contracts in the U.S. in over a century.
Mansour grew up in Lebanon and met his cofounder, Luana Lopes Lara, while studying computer science at MIT.
He owns an estimated 12% stake in Kalshi.

name: Yusuf Hamied
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Yusuf Hamied is the non-executive chairman of Mumbai-based generics maker Cipla.
Cipla was founded in 1935 by his father Khwaja Abdul Hamied, a disciple of Mahatma Gandhi.
After the patriarch passed away in 1972, Cambridge-educated Hamied and his brother Mustafa inherited the business.
Hamied took on big pharmaceutical companies, offering low-cost generic drugs for diseases such as AIDS, earning the label of drug pirate.
At the annual shareholders' meeting in 2023, Hamied called reports of a potential stake sale in Cipla by the family to a private equity firm as "speculative."
forbes_facts: His niece Samina Hamied was Cipla's executive vice-chairman until March 2024.
Renowned music conductor Zubin Mehta is Hamied's childhood pal.
Cambridge University has named a building after him, making him the first Indian to get that honor.

name: Wesley Edens
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Wes Edens cofounded asset manager Fortress Investment Group in 1998.
A former BlackRock partner, Edens first became a billionaire alongside his four cofounders when Fortress went public in 2007.
Fortress was acquired by SoftBank in 2017 for $3.3 billion. Edens walked away with about $500 million pretax.
He is the CEO of publicly traded liquefied natural gas company New Fortress Energy.
He is a co-owner of the NBA's Milwaukee Bucks, Premier League soccer team Aston Villa and Portugal's Vitoria Club Sport soccer club.
His Brightline railway, the only private passenger line in the U.S., operates high-speed trains from Orlando to Miami.
forbes_facts: Edens began construction on Brightline West, his second railway, in 2024. The $12 billion project line will be the first true high-speed train in the U.S.

name: David Fong
forbes_bio: David Fong is the managing director and co-chairman of Hip Shing Hong Group, one of Hong Kong's largest private real estate investment companies.
His late father Fong Yun Wah served as chairman of the group until 2022. His uncle is now co-chairman.
The family had an early sesame-seed-processing business, which eventually gave way to property investment and Hip Shing Hong started in 1948.
Today the group's businesses span across residential, commercial and hospitality.
David's son Jonathan is deputy managing director of the group; younger son Vincent runs his own business in healthtech.
forbes_facts: The company's roots date back to 1927, when Fong Yun Wah arrived in Hong Kong with his father from Guangdong province.

name: Ed Craven
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Wikidata (2024)
forbes_bio: Ed Craven and Bijan Tehrani founded and run Stake.com, believed to be the largest crypto-backed online casino in the world.
Stake.com generated $4.7 billion of gross revenue in 2024, despite crypto gambling being unavailable in the United States, United Kingdom and much of Europe.
The founders have reinvested its profits into aggressive marketing, putting Stake's name on Formula 1 cars, English Premier League jerseys, UFC octagons and a new livestreaming service.

During the pandemic, Stake started paying content creators on Twitch millions to livestream themselves gambling, transforming the business from $100 million in revenue to over $2 billion in two years.
After Twitch banned Stake from advertising on its platform due to a lack of consumer protections, Craven and Tehrani launched their own competing livestream service, Kick.
forbes_facts: Craven and Tehrani first met online as teenagers, playing the videogame "Runescape." The name Stake comes from the controversial "Runescape" game mechanic called "staking."

name: Agoes Projosasmito
forbes_bio: Agoes Projosasmito is the president commissioner of Amman Mineral Internasional, one of the largest copper-and-gold mining companies in Indonesia.
He owns a minority stake in the firm, which went public on the Indonesia stock exchange in 2023 raising $710 million.

Projosasmito also owns stakes in Indonesian oil and gas company Medco Energi Internasional, coal miner Bumi Resources and its mining subsidiary Bumi Resources Minerals where he sits as president director.

Projosasmito claims to be a trusted ally of Indonesian billionaire Anthoni Salim. Their relationship started in 1989 when he helped with the IPO of Salim's cement company, Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa.
He has more than three decades of experience in capital  market and extensive experience in the mining industry.
